steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease 18 muffin cups or line with paper liners.

Whisk flour, brown sugar, white sugar, baking powder, cinnamon, ginger, baking soda, salt, and nutmeg together in a bowl; form a well in center. Stir milk, melted butter, and beaten eggs into the well until smooth. Stir in cranberries, apple, hazelnuts, and figs until incorporated. Spoon batter into the prepared muffin cups, filling each about ¾ full.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into muffins comes out clean, 15 to 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Autumn Muffins
raw_recipe.description: This autumn muffin recipe features apples, cranberries, figs, and hazelnuts, and is spiced with cinnamon, nutmeg, and ginger for a fragrant, sweet treat.

review.reviewBody:
When I found this recipe, I was looking for something with apples and spices. This is perfect! The only change that I have made is to substitute applesauce for the butter. It makes them a little bit moister and a lot less fat and calories. I always get such compliments on these. Thanks!
Leslie

Tweaked it...loved it! Used toasted walnuts instead of hazelnuts, which I never have on hand, and used 1/2 cup melted unsalted butter and 1/2 cup applesauce instead of 1 cup melted butter. Grated the apple instead of chopping it. Also increased amounts of chopped fresh cranberries and dried figs once batter was complete as our crew likes lots of goodies in their muffins. Topped batter in one muffin pan with raw/turbinado sugar for a sweet 'n crunchy topping. We're working on those first as I find the surface of stored baked goods with sugar topping tends to get 'wet' as the sugar dissolves from the moisture in the baked goods. Baked in 2 silicone large-size muffin pans (got 12 muffins out of the batch) for 23 minutes. Whatever is leftover will be frozen individually for grab-n-go breakfasts. It shouldn't take them all that long to thaw. I think I want to try chopped banana in the next batch. Yum!

The recipe made so much batter that I ended up making it as two loaves of bread. I knew we'd never eat that many muffins between 2 of us. I only used fresh apple and fresh cranberries, and substituted oat meal for 1/3 of the flour (to increase the fiber). I used apple sauce for the butter, I also threw in some milk chocolate chips just before I poured the batter into 2 pans.

Love this recipe...however made a few changes. I revised the recipe somewhat. No fat at all. Added 1 cup of applesauce instead. Did not use any white sugar at all, as the sauce was sweet enough. Added 1 1/2 cup shredded zucchini. The only fruit I used was the chopped apple and instead of cranberries used raisins. No nuts. I brushed the muffin tins with coconut oils and discovered how easily the muffins slipped out of the pan. I've found that when I don't use fat in my muffin recipes, the muffins always stick to the tin. Not this time. (Happy dance). The muffins are moist, albeit slightly chewy. I put this down to no fat. Also, after reading many reviews an underlying theme was that the muffins were crumbly. Mine are not. I looked at the time for cooking! Mine were done in 19 minutes, so am wondering if the 30 minutes makes them overdone? At any rate, I started checking them after 16 minutes. Perfectly baked. As to freezing....I always freeze muffins and have never had a problem, so will be testing these as to whether or not they freeze well. I don't see a proble, but one never knows. And, btw.......if you're worried about 304 calories per muffin, half the sugar, and no fat brings them down to 150-160 calories per muffin. With minimal fat....oh and nice rise to the muffin....
I’ll grate the apple (large holes), use toasted walnuts, dried dates and dried cranberries, and I’ll add ground cardamom because I’m addicted to it and the flavor is perfect.

Wonderful muffins! I subbed 1/2c applesauce for 1/2c of the butter. Forgot the nutmeg; it was excellent without it. Takes awhile to prep the nuts and cranberries but that could be done ahead of time. It's definitely worth the time to toast the hazelnuts.

Delicious! I shredded my apples,as someone suggested and that worked nicely. I thought the Gala apples were a little bland, so I'll try Fuji apples next time. I used walnuts because those are the only nuts my husband likes. At the last minute, I used dates instead of figs because the dates were already chopped and my back was starting to ache. I would like even more cranberries, dates or figs, and nuts, so I'll increase them next time. Also, they tend to sink in the batter, so I recommend to keep stirring while filling the muffin tins. I did have to bake them for 25 minutes.

Really good with agave nectar instead of brown sugar, grated ginger, frozen blueberries instead of cranberries and roasted walnuts. I made them in big muffins molds so it took longer to bake. The dried figs in the muffins are a very good idea.

These are hands-down, absolutely, positively, without-a-doubt the BEST MUFFINS I HAVE EVER HAD IN MY ENTIRE LIFE. I cannot believe how freaking delicious these muffins really are. I did not change a single thing about this recipe (although I do use unbleached whole-wheat flour), and they came out absolutely perfect. In fact, I ended up with 28 muffins and I don't think I'll have a problem getting rid of them because they're so absolutely scrumptious. 

The texture is lovely, they are moist, fluffy and they are not too heavy. Next time, I will use a granny smith apple to add a bit more tang.

So fantastic, thank you for sharing this recipe!


Edit: I made these muffins again and I used a granny smith apple. My GOD, they are simply amazing. This time around, I whipped up some crumble topping for them and it was exactly what they needed. I am bringing these to a picnic tomorrow and I know my friends will be NUTS for them!

As others have, I did the following substitutions:

applesauce for butter 
almond milk for Milk 
Stevia Extract for sugar
Gluten Free Flour for wheat based flour

added an extra tsp of baking power

I did not have figs so just used an apple, dried cranberries and used the following mix for the nuts: 1/2 pecans and 1/2 hazelnuts

I surprised my self how good they turned out.

Update - I did freeze a bunch of these - since it made two dozen. We pulled some out and they were just as good as the day I made them - so they appear to freeze well. I froze them individually and then placed them into a freezer bag.

These were moist and very good. I did use coconut oil instead of butter which may have changed the texture. 
I used craisens and walnuts and they were delicious. I'm going to try some dates next time. I think the basic recipe has a lot of possibilities.

Update I did make them with the dates added, everybody has loved them! I think the blend of the sweetness of the date and citrus of craisin makes a very tasty muffin. also One reviewer said she didn't think they freeze well, but I have Frozen them and they're just fantastic! that could be because I used to the dried fruit, not fresh.
I loved the spices and fruits and nuts! I cut the sugar to 1/2 cup of each, used 1/2 c applesauce & 1/2 cup butter. very refreshing because it was not sweet.

I thought they were absolutely wonderful! Nuts and fruits go great together. I did not use figs, but raisins instead. I did not tweak it with other flours. I added extra Cinnamon and used walnuts or pecans. They were nice and moist. I will keep this recipe.
Absolutely delish - wouldn't change a thing.
So yummy! This recipe is so easy to modify but great as is.

These muffins are outstanding. I had to make a couple of substitutions as I didn’t have hazelnuts, used walnuts. Had no figs so I used dried fruit that came in a Christmas basket, used few dates, apricots & prunes. I have no interest in making healthier, I just like good food....this wins the prize.
I left out the figs, but these are delicious. Taste like autumn.

I used only Whole Dried Cranberries instead of fresh cranberries and also diced apples. I did not add any other fruits or nuts. They were totally amazing ! They rose higher in the muffin pans than any muffins I have ever made, and were very delicious. I think you could use just about any fruit in this recipe, although the batter was very thick , so perhaps delicate fruits like fresh blueberries or raspberries would not stand up as well. I will try it again with figs, or dates and nuts. I will definitely make this again.
These were amazing! I made these in the spring, so there weren’t any fresh cranberries on the shelves. However, if you soak craisins in hot water, they’ll work just fine.
works with dried apricots, toasted almonds, raisins, whatever. The hint of ginger is the magic ingredient!
